asis-charcoal: Activated charcoal can help gut toxicity, but it adsorbs drugs. Sometimes that is exactly the point. It can also flatten or reduce a trip, so I don't treat charcoal and zeolite as interchangeable. When the goal is to reduce drug absorption or stop a toxic gut situation, charcoal may be relevant. When I want to preserve the trip while improving the gut feeling, I prefer zeolite. Charcoal can also adsorb medications somebody depends on. I would use it cautiously around necessary medicines and tell the medics if charcoal was taken.

Most sober people don't feel much from zeolite, but its effect becomes more obvious when a trip has a toxic or gut-driven component.
I put a spoonful of zeolite into a cup of water or juice and sip slowly (some people need a teaspoon, others a tablespoon). Rubbing the zeolite on the body or simply holding the jar also helps me.
In my experiments, zeolite has to be prepared correctly. I use powdered zeolite rather than nano-liquid zeolite.
Many products did nothing for me, and quality mattered enormously.
Most zeolites have clogged pores because they haven't been cleaned, but ZeoCharge is sold as cleaned.

With a machine producing about two grams of ozone per hour, ten minutes produced a working zeolite for me.
Less time did not work as well, and more time did not noticeably improve it.

I also keep zeolite away from metal during preparation, so I use glass for ozonating and storing it whenever possible. Zeolite binds metals, which is part of why it is used for heavy-metal removal, so I don't put it into a metal thing or use a metal spoon.
